accepted_units.title: Endpoint transport plans lift to distributions over geodesic paths
accepted_units.why_material: A coupling records where mass starts and ends but not which minimizing paths it follows. A measurable geodesic selection lifts an optimal coupling to a dynamical plan, and evaluating that plan at each time produces a curve whose length equals the endpoint Wasserstein distance.
accepted_units.context_note: The source proves the measurable-selection construction and the length identity; the planar switch example only illustrates nonuniqueness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Compactness and the length-space property ensure minimizing geodesics and measurable selection; quadratic cost and constant-speed parametrization give the exact length calculation.

accepted_units.title: Every Wasserstein geodesic is reconstructed by dyadic gluing and compactness
accepted_units.why_material: Optimal couplings between successive dyadic-time marginals are glued into compatible finite path laws; equality in the metric bounds forces the glued points onto minimizing geodesics, and weak compactness yields one dynamical plan realizing every time marginal.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a theorem proved in the source, not merely cited background. Dense dyadic formulas are readable at the argument level but need visual checking for exact indices.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof uses disintegration/gluing, equality cases of triangle and quadratic bounds, compactness of the geodesic-path space, and continuity from dyadic to all times.

accepted_units.title: Approximation and lower semicontinuity extend weak convexity beyond regular endpoints
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates convexity along every geodesic from existence of one good geodesic and from restrictions to absolutely continuous endpoints, then proves that weak convexity on regular densities extends to arbitrary supported measures by energy-preserving approximation, geodesic compactness, and lower semicontinuity.
accepted_units.context_note: The definition includes the singular part of the energy and makes the quantifier distinction explicit. The approximation and lower-semicontinuity inputs are proved later in appendices.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extension relies on compact Wasserstein geometry, continuous-density approximation preserving the chosen energy, and lower semicontinuity; it does not upgrade the existential geodesic quantifier to all geodesics.

accepted_units.title: Local geodesic uniqueness upgrades weak convexity to all-geodesic convexity
accepted_units.why_material: If short subsegments of each geodesic are uniquely minimizing, the existential good geodesic between nearby points must coincide with the chosen subsegment; local convexity then patches across the full interval.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem states separate versions for all measures and for a totally convex absolutely continuous subspace.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The upgrade materially requires local uniqueness, full support of the reference, and total convexity in the absolutely continuous version; without them weak and strong displacement convexity remain distinct.

accepted_units.title: Geodesic convexity yields transport-information-energy inequalities
accepted_units.why_material: A single convexity inequality along a geodesic from a measure to the reference gives a transport lower bound and, by estimating the initial directional slope through a dynamical plan, a generalized HWI inequality linking energy, Wasserstein distance, and Fisher information.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof avoids an explicit derivative by convex comparison, monotonicity, Cauchy-Schwarz, and a descending metric gradient. Formula-heavy estimates require exact visual verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The slope estimate needs a positive Lipschitz density, regularity of the convex integrand, absolute continuity along the selected geodesic, and the dynamical-plan representation.

accepted_units.title: Approximate metric equivalences lift quantitatively to Wasserstein spaces
accepted_units.why_material: Pushing measures forward along an approximate isometry distorts quadratic transport costs by a controlled amount, while an approximate inverse supplies the reverse estimate and approximate surjectivity; therefore convergence of compact spaces induces convergence of their Wasserstein spaces.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is internal to the source. The displayed distortion constant is extraction-sensitive but the two-sided comparison mechanism is clear.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Compactness controls diameters, pushforward transports couplings, and approximate inverses are required for the reverse bound and density of the image.

accepted_units.title: Weak displacement convexity survives measured Gromov-Hausdorff limits
accepted_units.why_material: Regular endpoint measures are pulled back to approximating spaces, good geodesics are compactified after pushforward, endpoint energies converge, and contraction plus joint lower semicontinuity pass the convexity inequality to the limit; the same geodesic can be retained for an entire family of energies.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a central theorem proved in the source, with the family-valued version and regular-endpoint equivalence stated explicitly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof depends on measured convergence of references, Wasserstein-space convergence, energy contraction under pushforward, joint lower semicontinuity, and a common-geodesic quantifier for all functions in the family.

accepted_units.title: Dimension-indexed convex energies encode a synthetic curvature condition
accepted_units.why_material: A change of variables selects nested classes of convex internal energies indexed by a dimension parameter; weak simultaneous displacement convexity for the class becomes the definition of lower synthetic Ricci curvature, with pressure criteria giving equivalent membership tests.
accepted_units.context_note: The source proves nesting and pressure characterizations before using the classes in the definition. Exact derivative and exponent formulas are formula-risk points.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The encoding depends on the reference measure, Wasserstein geodesics, the dimension-indexed rescaling of density, and an existential common geodesic for the full energy class.

accepted_units.title: Synthetic curvature localizes to totally convex subsets and is closed under measured limits
accepted_units.why_material: Restriction to a totally convex subset preserves admissible geodesics, while renormalizing the restricted reference induces a corresponding rescaling of every energy; the main limit theorem then follows directly from family-wise displacement-convexity stability.
accepted_units.context_note: Both localization and measured-limit preservation are theorems proved here; the later smooth section separately checks agreement with classical curvature.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Localization requires total convexity rather than ordinary convexity and correct reference normalization; limit closure inherits all hypotheses of the measured Gromov-Hausdorff stability theorem.

accepted_units.title: Entropy convexity forces nonatomicity, volume growth, and precompactness
accepted_units.why_material: Transporting a point mass into a ball and comparing upper entropy convexity with support-based lower bounds rules out isolated partial atoms and yields a Bishop-Gromov-type ball-volume ratio; the growth bound then supplies metric-measure sequential compactness and full support of limits.
accepted_units.context_note: The proofs are internal. Concrete radii are symbolic parameters, not hidden arithmetic; dense Hölder and entropy formulas need visual checking.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conclusions use finite dimension-indexed entropy, displacement interpolation support contraction, nonatomicity or the delta case, full support for compactness, and the prior stability theorem.

accepted_units.title: Invariant lifting identifies quotient Wasserstein geometry and transfers curvature
accepted_units.why_material: Averaging couplings over a compact group and measurably choosing minimum-distance orbit representatives proves that invariant measures upstairs are isometric to all measures downstairs; uniqueness makes the lifted geodesic invariant, so its energy convexity descends to the quotient.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is proved under explicit uniqueness and absolute-continuity assumptions; it is not an unconditional quotient principle.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction requires a compact group with Haar measure, isometric measure-preserving action, measurable orbit representatives, unique absolutely continuous Wasserstein geodesics, and equality of lifted and quotient densities.

accepted_units.title: A tailored superlinear energy keeps interpolation inside the absolutely continuous class
accepted_units.why_material: Uniform integrability is converted into one admissible superlinear convex energy finite at both endpoints; convexity keeps that energy finite along a selected geodesic, and its infinite recession slope excludes singular mass. Approximation then shows that the reference support is geodesically convex and carries the same curvature condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The source constructs the energy using a convex minorant and proves both absolute-continuity and support results. Formula details around the minorant require verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This argument uses finite dimension parameter, simultaneous convexity for the full energy class, Dunford-Pettis uniform integrability, and closedness of the support under weak limits.

accepted_units.title: Synthetic curvature propagates through HWI to log-Sobolev, transport, and Poincaré bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The general geodesic HWI estimate is specialized using curvature-selected entropy and absolute continuity, yielding log-Sobolev and Talagrand inequalities; a small perturbation around the reference measure linearizes log-Sobolev into Poincaré.
accepted_units.context_note: The main implications and perturbative proof are internal. Some stronger cross-implications are explicitly announced for other work and remain cited/background rather than established here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The chain uses positive curvature for coercive constants, Lipschitz positive densities for Fisher information, the descending gradient norm, and a Taylor expansion near equilibrium.

accepted_units.title: Finite-dimensional entropy bounds yield Sobolev control and a curvature-growth diameter estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Reparameterizing the finite-dimension entropy inequality produces a Sobolev-type embedding estimate, while combining polynomial volume growth with transport concentration gives a weak Bonnet-Myers diameter bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The source proves the algebraic reformulation and invokes an earlier argument for the final universal diameter constant; the exact exponents and constant are formula-sensitive.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Sobolev exponents depend on the finite dimension parameter, and the diameter conclusion needs both finite-dimensional nonnegative curvature, positive infinite-dimensional curvature, and full support.

accepted_units.title: A root-Jacobian differential inequality compresses sectional data to Ricci curvature
accepted_units.why_material: Jacobi fields along an optimal transport map turn the determinant of its differential into a scalar function; self-adjoint matrix evolution and a trace inequality bound the second derivative of its normalized determinant by Ricci curvature.
accepted_units.context_note: This lemma is proved in the source and is the local engine for the smooth equivalence theorem. Matrix indices, determinant roots, and signs require PDF verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof requires a smooth manifold, almost-everywhere Hessian of the transport potential, nonsingular transport differentials, Jacobi equations, and self-adjointness of the induced deformation.

accepted_units.title: Weighted Ricci tensors are equivalent to displacement convexity of entropy
accepted_units.why_material: A change-of-variables formula factors transported densities into weighted Jacobian terms whose concavity, supplied by the curvature tensor bound, makes every admissible entropy convex; conversely, localized transports with chosen Hessian recover each tensor component from required entropy convexity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central smooth theorem proved in the source. It distinguishes the finite-dimension and infinite-dimension cases and handles the dimension obstruction explicitly; the derivation is densely formula-dependent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equivalence uses unique smooth-manifold optimal transport from absolutely continuous data, weighted Jacobians, the preceding Jacobi lemma, precisely chosen convexity classes, and localized test transports.

accepted_units.title: Limit stability and lifted geodesics transfer smooth and quotient curvature structure
accepted_units.why_material: Combining synthetic limit closure with smooth tensor equivalence characterizes smooth measured limits; invariant and horizontally lifted transport geodesics then transfer entropy convexity, hence curvature, through compact quotients and suitable Riemannian submersions.
accepted_units.context_note: Some partial converses use a cited warped-product construction, and one Alexandrov extension is explicitly conjectural; those statuses are retained rather than folded into the proved transfer mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The deductions require smoothness when returning to tensors, measured rather than bare metric convergence, invariant fiber measures, and horizontal lifts preserving Wasserstein length and entropy densities.

accepted_units.title: Sectional curvature lifts to Alexandrov curvature of Wasserstein space
accepted_units.why_material: A Lipschitz test function gives a dual lower bound on Wasserstein distance along any dynamical plan; for a nonnegatively curved manifold, coupling transported images from a common source bounds comparison angles by angles in an ambient Hilbert space, proving nonnegative Alexandrov curvature of Wasserstein space, with delta measures giving the converse.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem and supporting distance lemma are proved in the source. The gradient-flow remark at the end is a cited consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The forward implication relies on unique Monge representations from an absolutely continuous common source, sectional hinge comparison, density of that subspace, and completion; the converse uses the totally geodesic delta embedding.

accepted_units.title: Transport-potential angles identify Wasserstein tangent cones with Hilbert completions
accepted_units.why_material: Upper curvature comparison and a Lipschitz dual lower bound show that the angle between Wasserstein geodesics equals the normalized inner product of their transport-potential gradients; completing admissible potentials under the induced quadratic form yields the tangent cone as an inner-product space.
accepted_units.context_note: The source proves the angle identity and tangent-cone identification under nonnegative sectional curvature; heat-flow approximation is used to enlarge semiconcave potentials to all Lipschitz functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The identification is at absolutely continuous measures and uses Monge potentials, the source measure in the quadratic form, sectional/Alexandrov lower curvature, and completion modulo the zero-gradient kernel.

accepted_units.title: Legendre duality proves joint lower semicontinuity and contraction of convex measure energies
accepted_units.why_material: The nonlinear energy, including singular mass, is represented as a supremum of affine measure functionals using truncated subgradients and continuous approximation; this immediately gives joint lower semicontinuity and a data-processing inequality under measurable pushforward.
accepted_units.context_note: The full representation and consequences are proved here. The long truncation argument is formula-dense but its roles—capture singular mass, approximate measurably, then pass to continuous tests—are clear.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The result uses convex lower-semicontinuous integrands, Lebesgue decomposition, Legendre conjugacy, compact Hausdorff regularity, Lusin approximation, and bounded test functions below the recession slope.

accepted_units.title: Partition-of-unity kernels smooth measures without increasing convex energy
accepted_units.why_material: Symmetric local Markov kernels built from partitions of unity converge to the identity, produce continuous densities, and decrease every convex density energy by Jensen; lower semicontinuity then forces exact energy convergence to the original measure.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem handles absolutely continuous, singular, and mixed measures separately and is proved in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Compactness supplies finite partitions, symmetry preserves total mass, locality gives weak convergence, and the singular term is controlled by the recession slope of the convex integrand.

accepted_units.title: Formal Wasserstein Hessians expose the curvature-displacement-convexity correspondence
accepted_units.why_material: Representing a tangent direction by a continuity equation and using the formal Wasserstein geodesic equation turns the second derivative of a density energy into Hessian, weighted Ricci, and pressure terms, motivating why curvature-dimension inequalities imply geodesic convexity.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly says these calculations are purely formal and ignore regularity. This unit records a conceptual derivation only, not an independently rigorous theorem, and the equations have high extraction risk.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The calculation assumes smooth densities, potentials, integration by parts, Otto's formal metric, and unproved differentiability along formal geodesics; rigorous conclusions come from the separate smooth theorem.

accepted_units.title: Moment tightness replaces global compactness in noncompact Wasserstein geometry
accepted_units.why_material: On complete locally compact length spaces, finite second moments define the correct Wasserstein topology; endpoint tightness gives tightness of dynamical plans, and a uniform tail estimate places every geodesic between a compact set of endpoints inside one compact subset of Wasserstein space.
accepted_units.context_note: The extension of geodesic reconstruction and the compact-control proposition are proved here. A later remark about infinite-cost transport is background only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument needs completeness, local compactness of geodesic path sets, finite second moments, proper endpoint control, and the Wasserstein compactness criterion rather than compactness of the whole state space.

accepted_units.title: Growth conditions make convex energies and their approximation well-defined for infinite references
accepted_units.why_material: Polynomial or exponential growth classes for a nonfinite reference guarantee the negative part of admissible energies is integrable; weighted Legendre tests restore lower semicontinuity and contraction, while localized mollification and cutoff preserve both second moments and energy.
accepted_units.context_note: The source proves the well-definedness and sketches precise modifications of the compact duality/approximation proofs. Long weighted inequalities and exponents require visual verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The admissible growth rate is tied to the dimension-indexed convexity class, the topology uses weighted continuous functions, pushforwards need two-sided coarse growth bounds, and cutoffs must control second moments.

accepted_units.title: Proper pointed control extends curvature stability and passes it to tangent cones
accepted_units.why_material: A strengthened pointed convergence condition prevents mass from escaping through the comparison maps and supplies weighted reference convergence; compactly supported endpoint approximations and uniform moment tails recover a compact arena for the earlier limit proof, after which rescaling passes curvature to measured tangent cones.
accepted_units.context_note: The stability theorem is proved for finite dimension under the stated proper topology; the tangent-cone corollary additionally uses volume growth and requires the declared dimension range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The result depends on proper coarse bounds for comparison maps, weighted measured convergence, compactly supported density approximation, uniform second-moment tails, finite-dimensional volume growth, and subsequential pointed limits.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source repeatedly turns geodesic convexity into existence, stability, analytic bounds, support barriers, and dual lower-semicontinuity statements. This reinforces the routed lens within the isolated source; novelty and duplication were not compared.

Endpoint couplings, path measures, convex test potentials, invariant lifts, and weighted Legendre tests provide complementary objects for enforcing transport, marginal, quotient, and growth constraints. This is source-internal reinforcement only.

Smooth tensor conditions are re-expressed as convexity on a canonical probability-measure geometry, then transported through measured limits, supports, quotients, submersions, and tangent-cone constructions. No cross-corpus novelty claim is made.
